questions._figure: REQUIRED — BOTH sub-parts are printed as DRAWINGS, and the ring type IS the discrimination. ⚠ This typesetter distinguishes three ring kinds and all three appear on this page; each was verified at 10x. questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.context:
Transition metals have incomplete d-subshell either in neutral atom or in their ions. The presence of partly filled d-orbitals in their atoms makes transition elements different from that of the non-transition elements. With partly filled d-orbitals, these elements exhibit certain characteristic properties such as display of a variety of oxidation states, formation of coloured ions and entering into complex formation with a variety of ligands. The transition metals and their compounds also exhibit catalytic properties and paramagnetic behaviour. The transition metals are very hard and have low volatility. An examination of the \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{M^{2+}/M}}\) values shows the varying trends :

|  | \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{M^{2+}/M}}\) |
|---|---|
| V | \(-1{\cdot}18\) |
| Cr | \(-0{\cdot}91\) |
| Mn | \(-1{\cdot}18\) |
| Fe | \(-0{\cdot}44\) |
| Co | \(-0{\cdot}28\) |
| Ni | \(-0{\cdot}25\) |
| Cu | \(+0{\cdot}34\) |
| Zn | \(-0{\cdot}76\) |

questions.context: Carbohydrates are essential for life in both plants and animals. Carbohydrates are used as storage molecules as starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Chemically they are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. On the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, i.e., they are oxidized by Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. A monosaccharide like glucose is aldohexose and its molecular formula was found to be \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). After reacting with different reagents like HI, \(\mathrm{H_2N - OH}\), Bromine water, \(\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}\), etc. its structure was found to contain one aldehyde group, one primary alcoholic group, \((-\mathrm{CH_2OH})\) and four secondary alcoholic groups \((>\mathrm{CHOH})\). Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give some of the reactions of aldehyde group like Schiff's test, \(\mathrm{NaHSO_3}\) addition. This explains the existence of glucose in two cyclic hemiacetal forms which differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C \(-\) 1.

Fructose, Sucrose, Lactose, Galactose

questions.context: Carbohydrates are essential for life in both plants and animals. Carbohydrates are used as storage molecules as starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Chemically they are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. On the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, i.e., they are oxidized by Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. A monosaccharide like glucose is aldohexose and its molecular formula was found to be \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). After reacting with different reagents like HI, \(\mathrm{H_2N - OH}\), Bromine water, \(\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}\), etc. its structure was found to contain one aldehyde group, one primary alcoholic group, \((-\mathrm{CH_2OH})\) and four secondary alcoholic groups \((>\mathrm{CHOH})\). Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give some of the reactions of aldehyde group like Schiff's test, \(\mathrm{NaHSO_3}\) addition. This explains the existence of glucose in two cyclic hemiacetal forms which differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C \(-\) 1.
questions.stem: Name the polysaccharide which is known as 'animal starch'. Why is it called 'animal starch' ?

questions.stem:
(i) Name the isomers of glucose which in the cyclic form differ only in the configuration of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group at C \(-\) 1.
(ii) Presence of which functional group was detected when glucose reacted with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) water ?
questions._flag: The paper labels BOTH branches of this choice '(c)'; there is no printed letter distinguishing them, so the ref/questionNumber carry an explicit 'OR' rather than an invented sub-label.

questions.stem:
(i) The resistance of \(0{\cdot}05\) M \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) solution is found to be 100 ohm. If the cell constant is \(0{\cdot}0354\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}\), calculate the molar conductivity of the acetic acid solution.
(ii) State Faraday's first law of electrolysis. How much charge in Faraday is required for the reduction of 1 mol of \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}}\) to \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\) ?

(i) The conductivity of \(0{\cdot}0025\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}\) acetic acid is \(5{\cdot}25 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}\). Calculate its degree of dissociation if \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{o}}_{\mathrm{m}}\) for acetic acid is \(390\ \mathrm{S\,cm^2\,mol^{-1}}\).
(ii) Write anode, cathode and overall reaction of lead storage battery.
questions._flag: Sub-part (ii) is a Batteries question while (i) is Conductance; the row is filed on Conductance, which carries 3 of the 5 marks.

questions.stem:
Answer any five of the following :
(a) How is the crystal field splitting energy for octahedral complex \((\Delta_{\mathrm{o}})\) related to that of tetrahedral complex \((\Delta_{\mathrm{t}})\) ?
(b) Write the IUPAC name of the following complex :
\(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2](NO_3)_2}\)
(c) Write the geometry and magnetic behaviour of the complex \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\) on the basis of Valency Bond Theory (VBT).
(d) What type of isomerism is shown by the complex \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]\,[Cr(CN)_6]}\) ?
(e) For the coordination compound on the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for \(\mathrm{d^4}\) ion if \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < \mathrm{P}\). Is the coordination compound a high spin or low spin complex ?
(f) Out of \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^{+}}\), which complex is heteroleptic and why ?
(g) Draw the structures of optical isomers of \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\).

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(i) Account for the following :
(1) Oxidation of aldehydes is easier as compared to ketones.
(2) The alpha \((\alpha)\) hydrogen atoms of aldehydes are acidic in nature.
(ii) Write the products in the following reactions :
(1) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOH}/\mathrm{I_2}} ? + ?\)
(2) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COCl} + \mathrm{(CH_3)_2Cd} \longrightarrow ? + \mathrm{CdCl_2}\)
(iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between ethanoic acid and ethanal.
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — Sub-part (ii) prints both substrates as DRAWINGS, not as the condensed formulae transcribed above: (1) a skeletal Kekule benzene ring with the label "COCH3" above it, arrow labelled "NaOH / I2" to "? + ?"; (2) a skeletal Kekule benzene ring with the label "COCl" above it, "+ (CH3)2Cd" then an arrow to "? + CdCl2". Page idx 24.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(i) Draw structure of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde.
(ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN :
\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\), \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C - COCH_3}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)
(iii) How can you convert phenyl magnesium bromide to benzoic acid ?
(iv) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzaldehyde and ethanal.
(v) Write the main product in the following reaction :
\(\mathrm{CH_3 - CO - CH_2 - COOC_2H_5} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ H^{+}}]{\mathrm{(i)\ NaBH_4}} ?\)
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — In sub-part (v) the substrate is printed as a TWO-DIMENSIONAL structure — the chain "CH3 - C - CH2 - COOC2H5" with a vertical double bond dropping from the second carbon to an O written beneath it — which the linear transcription above renders as the condensed "CH3 - CO - CH2 - COOC2H5". Faithful in identity, but not what the page looks like. Page idx 26.
